mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation or equivalent of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Company Registrar or Companies Registry in the foreign shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel path: if the document is issued in an Apostille Convention member state, notarize signatures as required, obtain a Hague Apostille from the designated Competent Authority of that state, arrange for a certified Korean/English translation, and submit the apostilled set to the Korean Commercial Registry and the presentation bank. If the document is issued in a non-member state, do not use an Apostille; instead notarize the document, then obtain sole consular legalization from the Republic of Korea embassy or consulate with jurisdiction, followed by certified translation. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and may never be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Existence of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Government authority in the country of incorporation, such as Secretary of State, Companies House, or provincial registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel path: for Apostille states, authenticate the certificate by obtaining a Hague Apostille from the Competent Authority of the issuing state after any required notarization, then obtain certified Korean/English translation and submit to the Korean registry and banks. For non-member states, use consular legalization solely through the Republic of Korea embassy or consulate with territorial competence. Never chain Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorizing incorporation of the Korean Chusik Hoesa and appointing the local representative and opening of bank accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors and corporate secretariat of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel path: in Apostille states, certify the Board Resolution by corporate secretary, notarize officer signatures if necessary, obtain a Hague Apostille, then prepare a certified Korean/English translation for submission. In non-Apostille states, notarize the resolution and then obtain consular legalization from the Republic of Korea embassy or consulate; do not add an Apostille. The two authentication methods are exclusive alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or Memorandum and Articles of Association of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretariat or registered office of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel path: in Apostille states, obtain a certified true copy, notarize the copy if required by the issuing state, attach a Hague Apostille, and provide a certified Korean/English translation. In non-Apostille states, authenticate the certified copy by consular legalization solely with the Republic of Korea embassy or consulate having jurisdiction, followed by certified translation; do not use Apostille in this sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter evidencing account history, creditworthiness and source of funds of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign bank or financial institution maintaining the foreign shareholder's operating and capital accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel path: for Apostille states, have the bank sign the reference letter before a notary or bank officer with lawful authority, obtain a Hague Apostille from the issuing state's Competent Authority, and then provide an officially certified Korean/English translation for the Korean bank and registry. For non-Apostille states, have the bank letter notarized and then obtain consular legalization from the Republic of Korea embassy or consulate; never add an Apostille to a consularized document.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Conduct enhanced due diligence on every shareholder, director, ultimate beneficial owner, authorized signatory, and counterparty benefitting from the anti-cheat engine, using a risk-based approach that screens against OFAC SDN and consolidated lists, UN Security Council sanctions, EU consolidated financial sanctions, HM Treasury, Korean Ministry of Economy and Finance/Sanctions lists, Interpol notices, and local regulatory enforcement databases. For all non-resident corporate shareholders, identify and verify each UBO at or above 25%, document source of funds for capital contributions, and perform adverse-media and PEP matching using reliable commercial databases, escalating any positive PEP or sanctions hit to the Korea FIU suspicious transaction reporting protocol under the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information within 24 hours where required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration System and the Commercial Registration Office of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be registered in Hangul script; an English transliteration may be used as a trade name only, while the official registered name remains the Korean Hangul name. The name must follow a four-tier sequence: distinctive title, business-purpose element describing the software development and gaming integrity services, corporate form Chusik Hoesa, and any branch or DBA marker. Foreign-language names must be transliterated phonetically into Hangul and must not create confusion with existing names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written correction or objection with the competent District Court registration officer within two weeks of the rejection notice, explaining why the proposed name is distinctive and not misleading. If the registration officer maintains the rejection, appeal to the Supreme Court of Korea through an administrative motion or obtain judicial review by applying to the competent District Court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act. The applicant may simultaneously reserve an alternative name to avoid operational delay while the appeal is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a Korean Chusik Hoesa engaged in B2B software middleware, the National Tax Service requires a physical place of business capable of storing books, records and computing equipment; a virtual office or mail-forwarding address alone will be rejected for the issuance of an electronic tax invoice and will cause bank account opening failure at regulated financial institutions. A semi-virtual serviced office with a physical rented desk, fixed-line telephone, and storage can be accepted, but Korean banks will inspect the lease and evidence of actual human employee presence. We recommend a physical one-person office lease registered at the local district office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) the Commercial Registration Office may send a representative to verify the registered office address; (2) National Tax Service field officers may inspect before issuing a business registration certificate and during VAT audits; (3) municipal tax authorities may verify place of business for local income tax and business place tax; (4) banks conduct on-site visits before corporate account activation. Quantified risk: 68% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months for a newly registered software company using a virtual or home address; 25% for a fully staffed standard leased office; 55% for serviced co-working space.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended) for the Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation), particularly Articles 288 (incorporation by promoters), 292 (contents of the Articles of Incorporation), 295 (payment of share value), 299 (judicial inspection of in-kind contributions), 301 (deposit of subscription price), 317 (registration of incorporation), 318 (office of registration), 329 (share capital and par value), 383 (appointment of directors), 389 (representative director), 393 (powers of the board of directors), 398 (self-dealing restrictions), and 434 (extraordinary resolution requirements); Foreign Exchange Transactions Act Articles 6 and 13; Foreign Investment Promotion Act Articles 2, 5, and 6; and the Corporate Registration Regulations promulgated by the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registration Office of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered head office address, operated by the Registry Division of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea; for Seoul-headquartered companies, the Seoul Central District Court Registration Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Korean-language Articles of Incorporation, the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Corporation (Chusik Hoesa), the Certificate of Deposit of Stock Subscription Price issued by a licensed Korean bank, and supporting resolutions and officer acceptances, resulting in the court-issued Certificate of Registered Matters.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital applies to an ordinary Chusik Hoesa under Article 329 of the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea. The Articles of Incorporation must state the total authorized shares and per-share par value, and par value may not be less than KRW 100 per share. The entire subscription price must be paid before registration and deposited in a blocked stock subscription account in the name of the company-in-formation or promoter at a Korean commercial bank; the deposit remains blocked until the bank receives the court-issued certificate of incorporation registration. The deposit certificate must be filed with the registry. In-kind contributions require a court-appointed inspector's report unless all promoters unanimously request exemption in notarized articles. Foreign investors must first report the investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and remit funds through a Korean foreign exchange bank.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation, CHUSIKHOESA (the 'Company'), a Chusik Hoesa stock corporation to be incorporated under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, hereby adopts, ratifies, and confirms the Articles of Incorporation executed by the promoters and subscribers, and all covenants, reservations, and procedures contained in such Articles are approved as the supreme internal governance charter of the Company. RESOLVED, that the authorized share capital of the Company is KRW [__] divided into [__] authorized ordinary shares, each with par value KRW [__]; of such authorized shares, [__] ordinary shares are subscribed and issued at incorporation, representing paid-in capital of KRW [__]; every issued share is fully paid in cash by the subscriber concerned in lawful Korean currency to the designated stock subscription account of the Company at a licensed Korean bank; and the Representative Director is directed to obtain and preserve the bank certificate of subscription deposit. RESOLVED, that the registered head office and principal place of business of the Company is established at [street address, city, province, postal code, Republic of Korea] (the 'Registered Office'); the Representative Director is empowered to execute, sign, seal, deliver, and file the lease, occupancy certificate, and related real estate documents with the competent District Court Registration Office and to cause the Registered Office to appear in all certificates, invoices, contracts, and statutory filings. RESOLVED, that the following persons are appointed as the statutory officers of the Company: [Name] as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; [Name] as Director; [Name] as Director; and [Name] as Auditor or Audit Committee member, as applicable; each such officer shall hold office until the first annual general meeting of shareholders following his or her appointment and until successors are lawfully elected and qualified. RESOLVED, that the Representative Director, together with any one other director, is authorized to open, maintain, direct, and close deposit accounts, corporate accounts, foreign currency accounts, and collection accounts with [Bank], to appoint and remove authorized signatories, to execute banking mandates, operating resolutions, and electronic banking agreements, and to issue irrevocable instructions for SWIFT-wire and other payment settlements related to subscription revenue from gaming anti-cheat middleware. RESOLVED, that the Representative Director and the directors are jointly and severally authorized to make all applications, submissions, registrations, and notifications required for corporate existence, including the incorporation registration, business license registration, foreign investment report confirmation, social insurance enrollment, tax registration, and all government authorizations necessary to conduct ISIC 6201 software development; and any lawful action taken by the officers before this resolution is ratified. RESOLVED, that any two directors, or the Representative Director together with the corporate seal, may execute any agreements, certificates, powers of attorney, immigration documents, and banking instructions to implement these resolutions. RESOLVED, that these resolutions are effective immediately and shall remain in force until amended or rescinded by a subsequent board resolution or general meeting of shareholders.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Notarization, and Foreign Investment Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Notary Public licensed under the Notary Act; Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) / Invest Korea for foreign investment report; or a Korean foreign exchange bank authorized to accept foreign investment reports.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation for the Chusik Hoesa. The object clause must be broad enough to cover computer programming, video game security middleware, kernel-level anti-cheat software development, licensing, sales, and support. Include the corporate name, address, authorized shares, par value, number of directors, and auditor provisions. Engage a Korean notary to notarize the adoption, verifying the identity of promoters and the sufficiency of the subscription plan. For non-resident owners, file the foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act with KOTRA or a foreign exchange bank before submission to the registry, obtain the report certificate, and prepare notarized English/Korean copies. Confirm that all founder names and passports correspond exactly to the articles to prevent registry rejection.
required_dossiers: Passport of each promoter or director
Proposed Korean Articles of Incorporation
Draft object clause for ISIC 6201 and NAICS 541511
Registered office address and lease or right-to-use evidence
Power of attorney if acting through an agent
Foreign investment report form and beneficial ownership declaration
Resume or identification of proposed directors and auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary rejects the articles or requests amendments, correct the defective provisions and re-notarize promptly. If KOTRA suspends the foreign investment report, cure the omissions through the Foreign Investment Support Center online portal and re-file within 15 days; if the foreign exchange bank declines, request written grounds and consult KOTRA's one-stop FDI service to obtain a validation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Blocked Stock Subscription Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed Korean commercial bank with corporate banking and foreign exchange dealing authorization, acting under Commercial Act Article 301.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional stock subscription account in the exact legal name of the future company, namely Chusikhoesa [Company Name] (Incorporation-Promoter) or in the promoter's name as permitted. Deposit the full statutory paid-in capital using lawful funds. For inbound foreign investment, ensure the remittance has a clear foreign investment report reference and route through a licensed foreign exchange bank. Obtain the bank certificate of deposit of subscription price indicating account name, amount, and date; keep this certificate in original form for the registry application. The account must remain blocked until the corporate registration certificate is presented. Complete the bank's AML/KYC, FATCA/Common Reporting Standard, and beneficial ownership certifications. After incorporation, convert the certificate into the company's permanent operating account only with a certified copy of corporate registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of Foreign Investment Report, if applicable
Stock subscription deposit application form
Passport and seal specimen of promoter
Bank AML/KYC and beneficial ownership declaration
Proof of address for the future head office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects account opening due to AML or tax information deficiencies, provide a notarized explanation and amend the forms. If the deposit certificate has a name mismatch with the future company, request the bank to reissue the certificate and correct the account name before the registration filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration with the District Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registration Office of the District Court of the Republic of Korea with jurisdiction over the registered head office, under the Supreme Court's Corporate Registration Regulations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation registration application to the corporate registration clerk. Attach the notarized articles, deposit certificate, appointment acceptances, and board resolutions. Pay the registration license tax and education surtax at the receipt office or through electronic stamping. The clerk will examine whether the formation satisfies Articles 288 through 317 of the Commercial Act; if all conditions are met, the court enters the company in the corporate registry and issues the Certificate of Registered Matters. The Representative Director must immediately verify entity name, registered capital, head office address, officers, and date. This entry is the legal birth of the separate limited liability entity. Also request the Certificate of Corporate Seal Impression at this time.
required_dossiers: Incorporation registration application form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of deposit of subscription price
Pro-forma board resolutions appointing officers
Written acceptance of office by each director and auditor
Foreign investment report certificate
Passport and power of attorney
Registration tax, education tax, and court fee payment vouchers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a correction order is issued, take corrective steps through the registry's electronic correction process within 14 days. If a definitive refusal is issued, request rehearing under the Non-Contentious Litigation Act or appeal to the appellate division of the District Court. If the refusal relates to a missing foreign investment report, obtain a corrected certificate from KOTRA and re-file with a letter explaining the cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business License, Tax Registration, Social Insurance, and Permanent Bank Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) district tax office via the HomeTax online portal; the local municipal or ward tax office for local taxes; the Social Insurance Information Service integrated portal for four major social insurance schemes; and a licensed Korean commercial bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the court registration, begin business formally by registering the taxable business with the district tax office and applying for a business registration certificate. The application must be made within the statutory period, generally within 20 days from business commencement, to avoid late-filing penalties. Simultaneously, enroll the company and its staff in national pension, health insurance, employment insurance, and industrial accident compensation insurance. Open the permanent corporate account at the bank, complete legal representative verification, and update the bank signatory list to match the registered directors. Register for VAT and corporate tax compliance matters and obtain any tax invoice or card approval. If the company will later process cross-border payments via SWIFT and Stripe, complete the bank's merchant account due diligence, agreeing to sanctions screening and transaction reporting.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate registration from the court
Certified corporate seal impression certificate
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Copy of lease agreement for the head office
Representative director's identification or passport
Foreign investment report certificate, if applicable
Bank account opening application and signatory mandate forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office has not assigned a business registration certificate within the expected window, visit the desk officer or use the HomeTax online inquiry. If a late filing penalty is assessed, file a request for reduction or abatement under the Framework Act on National Taxes and attach justification. If social insurance employer number issuance is delayed, contact the Social Insurance Information Service and provide corporate registration proofs.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - ISIC 6201 is a pure digital software activity under the Korean Standard Industrial Classification; no industrial licensing board, state manufacturing authority, or municipal physical plant agency has jurisdiction over the kernel-level anti-cheat engine middleware. If the entity later provides game services to the public in Korea, the Game Rating and Administration Committee (GRAC) may be relevant under the Game Industry Promotion Act, but that is outside the current B2B ISIC 6201 scope.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable for the anti-cheat engine B2B middleware. No manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehouse operating license is required. Any incidental game rating or game-providing business registration would be a separate

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr); customs export declarations and customs clearance through Korea Customs Service operating the UNI-PASS electronic clearance system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation) with potential foreign non-resident ownership, the company must first complete incorporation under the Korean Commercial Act and register the corporation with the court. Within 20 days after commencement of business, the company must file a business registration application with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the place of business, submitting the certificate of corporate registration, articles of incorporation, proof of address of the domestic registered office, director identification documents, and, for foreign investors without a domestic address or place of business, a validly appointed tax representative under the Framework Act on National Taxes. NTS then issues the 10-digit business registration number which serves as the corporate taxpayer identification number and VAT identification number. If the entity will export goods or services, it must separately register with Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS as an exporter and obtain the customs ID necessary for submitting export declarations and supporting electronic documentation. For non-resident foreign entities with no Korean establishment, registration is effected indirectly through the tax representative and HomeTax electronic authentication, and the NTS issues the tax identification code assigned to the foreign entity; the tax representative remains liable for procedural duties including filings, receipt of notices, and retention of records.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law provides no check-the-box election or elective hybrid mismatch regime. Entity classification as a domestic Chusik Hoesa is determined by the Korean Commercial Act and the Corporate Tax Act, with the corporation taxed at entity level on worldwide income. No alternative pass-through election is available for this corporate form.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean VAT Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory VAT registration is required within 20 days from commencement of business with no turnover threshold for general taxation; however, simplified taxable person status is available for businesses with taxable annual turnover below KRW 80,000,000, and the zero-rating and VAT refund regime remains available for qualifying exporters.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All Korean Vat-registered businesses must issue electronic tax invoices through the National Tax Service HomeTax system or NTS-certified ERP/API integration. Each electronic tax invoice must be transmitted to NTS no later than the day following issuance. There is no real-time fiscal clearance or mandatory cryptographic stamping requirement; anti-fraud enforcement relies on mandatory e-invoice transmission, real-time data matching with customs export records, and NTS data-analytic verification. Income and VAT filing must be submitted through HomeTax on a semi-annual VAT return basis, while export-related documentation must be retained and be available for electronic audit review.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exportation of goods from Korea and exportation of certain services used or consumed overseas qualify for zero-rating under the Korean VAT Act. For the gaming anti-cheat engine software and software-as-a-service supplied to non-resident customers, zero-rating is substantiated when the supply is deemed an export service under the VAT Act Enforcement Decree, the service is genuinely provided to a person outside Korea, the consideration is received in foreign currency, and documentary evidence proves the overseas use or consumption of the digital service. Goods exported must be cleared through Korean customs by filing an export declaration via UNI-PASS and the exporter must retain proof of foreign exchange receipt and logistics movement.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration submitted through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system (export clearance record showing HS code, value, destination, and exporter).

Commercial invoice and signed sales contract or license agreement with the overseas buyer identifying the anti-cheat engine or digital service, billing terms, and foreign currency settlement condition.

Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for physical goods; for digital services, a service delivery report or server-side electronic evidence showing the supply is received by the overseas customer outside Korea.
Inward Remittance Certificate or Foreign Exchange Transaction Report issued by a Foreign Exchange Bank in Korea evidencing that the foreign currency export proceeds have actually been repatriated.
Zero-rated e-Tax Invoice issued through HomeTax reflecting the export and the zero-rated VAT amount.
Where applicable, foreign exchange transaction confirmation from the payment rails (Swift Wire or Stripe payout) detailing the overseas settlement and FX conversion.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to strict post-clearance audit by the National Tax Service and Korea Customs Service. If any required documentation is missing, false, or fails to prove that the goods/services left Korea or the digital service was consumed overseas and that foreign currency was received within the 180-day repatriation deadline, the zero-rating is retrospectively disallowed, output VAT is assessed at the standard 10 percent rate, input VAT credits claimed in connection with the export supply are clawed back, and statutory penalty surcharges are imposed under the VAT Act and Framework Act on National Taxes. Fraudulent zero-rating claims, including fabricated export declarations or concealed foreign currency receipts, may additionally result in criminal indictment, fines, and imprisonment, and the NTS may reopen tax years beyond the ordinary five-year limitation period where willful evasion or omission of cross-border receipts is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) acting as the executing authority for foreign exchange policy delegated under the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) pursuant to the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a free-floating exchange rate regime with robust current-account convertibility. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, current-account payments such as software licensing royalties and gaming platform settlement revenues are freely convertible through registered foreign exchange banks, subject only to filing via the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) when transaction values exceed statutory reporting thresholds. Capital-account transactions, notably inbound equity injections into a Chusik Hoesa, are legalized through a mandatory registration and notification mechanism: a foreign investor must deposit capital into an account at a domestic licensed bank after filing a foreign investment notification, and the receiving bank verifies the purpose and source of funds. Profit remittance, including dividends, liquidation proceeds, and royalty payments, are permitted after the submitting entity provides evidence of the original foreign investment notification, payment of Korean corporate taxes, and source-country residency certification if a treaty benefit is claimed. However, Korean won is not freely deliverable offshore as a fully convertible clearing currency; non-resident KRW accounts are tightly managed and all outbound FX conversions require documented real demand. Banks further require compliance with Korean transfer-pricing regulations, which prevent synthetic profit extraction and meaningfully constrain international treasury structures. In practice, conversion hurdles are administrative rather than prohibitive, and a fully compliant foreign-invested entity can access capital-account and current-account convertibility within one to three banking days of filing, provided no AML or tax red flag is triggered.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must collect exported goods and service revenue within 18 months from the date of export declaration, with an extension to 20 months available for specific products approved by the Bank of Korea. There is no mandatory conversion ratio of foreign currency export proceeds into KRW; exporters may retain earned FX in a domestic foreign exchange account. However, the exporter must obtain a confirmation of receipt from an authorized foreign exchange bank within 30 days of collection, and the actual monetary settlement must be made through a licensed Korean bank to satisfy the ‘receipt and settlement’ obligation under current foreign exchange regulations. Failure to collect within the statutory period requires a prior approval or waiver from the competent foreign exchange bank, and the corresponding FEIS reporting record must be updated. This rule is particularly relevant for inbound licensing fees from international gaming platforms that use Stripe or SWIFT wires, since the collected foreign currency must be formally received and settled to the tax-paying Korean entity.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Investment) and Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW/USD)
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW/USD) with cross-border payment integration
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW/USD/JPY)
Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW/USD) – capital escrow not preferred
Operational Currency Account for SMEs and venture firms – capital escrow subject to branch discretion

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, and comparable providers are not licensed to operate as Korean banks and cannot legally maintain KRW settlement accounts, process domestic payments, or receive capital injections on behalf of a Korean resident legal entity. Under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, only banks that are licensed by the Korean Financial Services Commission can hold customer funds in domestic payment accounts and perform cross-border settlement as principals. An offshore EMI may only serve as an ancillary payable/receivable network to initiate funds transfers; all underlying clearing and conversion must traverse a domestic authorized foreign exchange bank. A Chusik Hoesa holding a gaming anti-cheat middleware business must therefore build its treasury on a direct relationship with a Tier-1 Korean commercial bank. Relying on a fintech EMI for capital subscription or operational disbursements creates serious AML exposure and regulatory risk for the entity and its directors.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, at least one statutory director or a designated signatory with a notarized power of attorney must appear physically in-branch for the initial corporate account onboarding and for signing the Korean bank’s signature specimens. Most Tier-1 Korean banks require the personal appearance of the legal representative from the certificate of incorporation, although remote video-based KYC is permitted for existing global-relationship clients of a bank’s overseas branch network. Consular proxy opening is rarely accepted as a substitute; when permitted, it is conditioned on a full apostilled corporate dossier, an in-person identity verification by a Korean consulate, and the submission of original power-of-attorney instruments. For a gaming anti-cheat engine company with low-risk intangible revenue, directors should budget for a brief Seoul visit to complete the statutory interview, produce valid passports, and execute a bank-specific compliance questionnaire. A domestic registered agent with a durable power of attorney may initiate the account-opening paperwork, but the banks will still require the UBO or statutory representative’s live video verification before activating the account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex multi-tier cross-border ownership in which a foreign ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) sits above an opaque intermediary jurisdiction, creating an elevated source-of-wealth risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Arias or notarized corporate organizational chart of all upstream shareholders; audited financial statements for the last two fiscal years for the UBO and intermediate entities; recent bank reference letters documenting the economic explanation for the structure; personal UBO identity pages and wealth declaration signed under penalty of perjury; incorporation certificates and register of directors and members for each holding vehicle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cybersecurity and anti-cheat middleware licensing is an intangible-heavy business model that can trigger excessive scrutiny about the fair value of software royalty inflows and the commercial rationale of the Korean entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed software licensing and commercial distribution agreements with game studios; a detailed end-to-end service description including development timelines and kernel-level technology documentation; independently supported revenue projections based on signed contracts or platform placements; employment and payroll records in Korea proving operational substance; IT asset and server procurement invoices that substantiate the software development and maintenance capacity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection for paid-in capital or equity investment is flagged as suspicious when no clear business valuation underpins the capital amount, particularly for early-stage gaming security firms with limited tangible assets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified external valuation report on the company’s intellectual property and equity issued by a licensed Korean CPA firm; detailed R&D cost breakdown and inventory of capitalised development costs; the Korean entity’s capital account ledger and bank transfers traceable to the original foreign investment notification; tax clearance certificates from the National Tax Service; a three-year cash flow and capital requirement model explained in the board resolution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high-frequency FX flows between foreign digital gaming platforms, KRW settlement, and outgoing license fees may appear inconsistent or high-velocity, raising banking suspicion of structuring or layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A whiteboard statement of the treasury flow with bank-generated FEIS reports and SWIFT MT103 reference numbers; customer invoices and receipts linked to platform revenue earned; copies of all contracts and rate cards with gaming clients; a quarterly rolling liquidity forecast broken down by counterparty; a written undertaking to comply with the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit’s suspicious transaction reporting obligations, including any threshold reporting protocols.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections must first be registered via the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) using an authorized Korean commercial bank. The investing party wires funds through SWIFT MT103 using a purpose code that reflects an equity contribution or foreign capital investment as mapped to the Bank of Korea’s Classification of Foreign Exchange Transactions. The funds must arrive at the Korean bank’s designated capital escrow account opened under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, after which the bank issues a capital verification confirmation and files the domestic foreign-investment report with MOEF and BOK. A Korean CPA must subsequently issue a statutory capital verification certificate for the paid-in capital amount. For later profit repatriation, the entity establishes an operational current account and submits board resolutions, executed financial statements, tax clearances, and evidence of the original capital registration to request dividend remittance. No conversion of foreign currency into KRW is permitted without first booking an inbound exchange counterparty with the same Korean bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operational trade payments, the Korean entity should use SWIFT MT103 for direct invoice settlements with foreign suppliers or customers, with purpose codes aligned to the underlying service or royalty stream. For larger procurement and project-based sales, commercial letters of credit (sight or usance) and documentary collections (D/P or D/A) are the preferred clearing rails to mitigate cross-border payment risk in intellectual-property heavy transactions. All outgoing payments require the attaching of underlying contracts and tax invoices, and any remittance exceeding KRW 100 million or equivalent may trigger enhanced FEIS reporting. For recurring low-ticket licensing fees to overseas game studios, the entity may integrate a licensed global payment service, but the actual clearing must settle through a Korean bank account and not through an offshore EMI. All outbound KRW conversions must satisfy real-demand documentation and are settled via the designated foreign exchange account through Korea-based clearing rails, typically covered by RTGS operations in KRW and SWIFT NET settlement in USD.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD forward contracts for current trade and investment exposures with maturity up to 12 months, subject to underlying transaction documentation under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in KRW for non-resident entities or domestic currency with synthetic swap offset; these can be traded with Korean banks but only under the domestic bank’s designated permission and EMF review
Cross-currency swaps between KRW and USD for medium-term debt or treasury management, requiring strong indication of the hedged asset or liability and MOEF authorization

FX options (call/spread combinations) on KRW for anticipated trade receivables and payables, permitted only when used for hedging and not for speculative purposes, with bank-approved product documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return for the closed fiscal year, including tax adjustment schedules, financial statements, and statutory audit report attachments when the external audit duty applies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end: by March 31 of the following year. For any other fiscal year-end: within 3 months after the fiscal year closes. A one-month extension is available under the Framework Act on National Taxes where the corporation maintains overseas business establishments or complex accounts.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and non-filing penalty additions under the Framework Act on National Taxes apply: 20 percent of unpaid tax for under-reported tax, 40 percent for fraudulent non-reporting or failure to file, 10 percent for failure to pay timely assessed tax, plus statutory daily overdue interest on the unpaid amount. Persistent non-payment triggers National Tax Service collection procedures, including seizure of bank accounts, receivables, and other property, and may lead to compulsory dissolution proceedings if the company ceases lawful registered-address maintenance under the Korean Commercial Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax return and settlement for the local income tax imposed on the national corporate income tax.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government having jurisdiction over the corporation's head office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end: by April 30 of the following year. For any other fiscal year-end: by the last day of the month following the statutory corporate income tax return deadline. If the national corporate tax filing is extended, the local income tax deadline is extended by the same period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local Tax Act delinquency surcharges apply: 20 percent of the under-reported or non-reported local income tax, 40 percent for fraudulent failure to report, and additional monthly late-payment penalties on unpaid local tax. Continued non-payment permits the competent local government to conduct compulsory collection through seizure of property and bank accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Appointment of an independent certified public accountant or audit firm, completion of the statutory external audit, delivery of the audit report to the board of directors and shareholders, and public disclosure through the Financial Supervisory Service DART system when external audit duty applies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service via the DART electronic disclosure system and the external auditor appointed under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The audit must be completed before the annual general meeting of shareholders; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the annual general meeting must be convened by June 30 of the following year. The company must submit the audit report and audited financial statements to the Financial Supervisory Service through DART within 2 weeks after receiving the audit report or within the period prescribed under the External Audit Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor, obstruction of audit procedures, or failure to disclose audit-related documents may result in administrative fines up to KRW 30 million, criminal penalties of up to 3 years imprisonment or fines up to KRW 50 million under the External Audit Act, and administrative sanctions including designation as an audit-deficiency company. Continued default may trigger suspension or dissolution measures under relevant capital markets and commercial registration rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Convening the annual general meeting of shareholders, approval of annual financial statements, appointment or re-appointment of directors and statutory auditors, and documentary recordation in the corporate minute books.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate governance records maintained at the registered office; no tax authority filing is required solely for the shareholder meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Under Article 365 of the Korean Commercial Act, the annual general meeting must be held within 6 months after the end of the fiscal year, i.e., by June 30 for a December 31 year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the annual general meeting within the statutory window does not by itself dissolve the company, but directors and the representative director may be subject to administrative fines. Repeated failure to maintain lawful corporate governance records and a valid registered office may be treated by the registration court as grounds for ex officio dissolution procedures under the Korean Commercial Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual maintenance and verification of the statutory corporate registers, shareholder ledger, director registers, minutes books, and security registers, together with registration-court filings for any director, capital, registered office, or share-structure changes that occurred during the fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Korean registration court and the shareholders, as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each registrable corporate change must be filed with the local registry court within 2 weeks from the occurrence of the triggering event. No standalone annual registry renewal filing applies to an ordinary unlisted Chusik Hoesa.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filings expose each responsible director to administrative fines under Korean commercial registration practice; defective or incomplete registers can impair share transfer effectiveness and evidentiary standing. Continued failure to maintain a lawful registered office can trigger the registration court's administrative strike-off or dissolution process under the Korean Commercial Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, an independent certified CPA audit is mandatory for a Korean Chusik Hoesa unless the company qualifies as a statutory small-company exemption. The audit exemption is unavailable, and an external audit is legally required, if any of the following quantitative thresholds is met in the immediately preceding fiscal year: total assets equal or exceed KRW 10 billion; annual revenue equals or exceeds KRW 10 billion; or the average headcount equals or exceeds 100 employees. The exemption is also denied for listed companies, financial companies, and companies that must be audited under other statutes. For a gaming anti-cheat middleware entity exceeding these balance-sheet, revenue, or headcount thresholds, the company must appoint one or more licensed Korean certified public accountants registered with the Financial Supervisory Service and must prepare audited financial statements presenting fairly the financial position in accordance with the applicable Korean accounting standards.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards are mandatory for listed companies and financial institutions. Unlisted non-financial Chusik Hoesa entities may apply either K-IFRS or the Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles for non-public entities, commonly referred to as K-GAAP. The chosen framework must be applied consistently on an accrual basis, and the corporate income tax return must reconcile book income to taxable income under the Corporate Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic of Korea does not currently maintain a general public beneficial ownership register requiring an annual UBO confirmation from every ordinary unlisted Chusik Hoesa. The company must, however, maintain an updated register of members identifying every shareholder, record share transfers in the shareholder ledger before a transferee is recognized as a member, and follow the registration window set out in the articles of incorporation; if the articles are silent, the Korean Commercial Act makes the share transfer effective against the company upon entry in the register of members. A transfer of shares or any change in shareholding must be updated in the statutory registers within 30 days or such shorter period as the company's articles require. If the company is a foreign-invested enterprise under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act because a non-resident holds at least 10 percent of the issued shares, holds a controlling interest, or exceeds the minimum foreign investment amount, the company and the foreign investor must file the applicable foreign-investment reporting and modification reports within 30 days after any relevant shareholding, capital, or management change, and must satisfy any regular foreign-invested enterprise business-status reporting obligations with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy or its designated agencies.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Statutory Auditors or Audit Committee Members
Register of Charges, Pledges, and Mortgages over the company's assets
Minute Book for Annual General Meetings
Minute Book for Board of Directors Meetings
Share Certificate Ledger and related share-transfer records where share certificates are issued
Books of Account and supporting vouchers required under the Korean Commercial Act

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per annum for a standard registered office and corporate secretarial retainer in Seoul or a major Korean business hub, excluding disbursements; premium foreign-owned or technology-sector service packages may range up to USD 4,000 per annum.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 30,000 for a certified CPA audit of a medium-sized unlisted technology company with total assets near the KRW 10 billion statutory threshold, depending on group complexity, revenue mix, financing structures, and whether K-IFRS or K-GAAP financial statements are required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% maximum national corporate income tax rate, plus a 10% local income tax surtax, producing an aggregate maximum effective rate of 27.5%; taxable income up to KRW 200 million is taxed at 10%, KRW 200 million to KRW 2 billion at 20%, KRW 2 billion to KRW 30 billion at 22%, and amounts above KRW 30 billion at 25%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korea grants a Restriction of Special Taxation Act R&D tax credit of up to 30% of qualifying R&D expenditure for large enterprises and 50% for SMEs; foreign-invested high-tech companies in Free Economic Zones may obtain a 5-year 50% corporate income tax reduction; patent box treatment is not generally available, but anti-cheat software development costs can be expensed or amortized and incremental research deductions may apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Primary form is the Corporate Tax Base and Tax Return (Corporate Income Tax Return), submitted electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with a semi-annual interim corporate prepayment filing during the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return must be filed within 3 months after the fiscal year ends. For a December 31 fiscal year, the statutory deadline is March 31 of the following year. Interim prepayments are due within 2 months after the first six months of the fiscal year, generally August 31 for calendar-year corporations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total Taxable Income for the fiscal year, derived by reconciling book income before tax to taxable income through tax law adjustments, non-taxable income, non-deductible expenses, and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned Chusik Hoesa, report all Korean-source revenue from the anti-cheat engine licensing activity and ensure intercompany royalty or service payments to the foreign parent are adjusted to arm's length. Foreign-source income of a Korean tax resident corporation is also reportable here; a non-resident corporation with only a Korean permanent establishment reports only income attributable to that permanent establishment. Include any transfer-pricing adjustment to the royalty paid to the foreign ultimate parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed Corporate Income Tax before tax credits, calculated by applying the statutory progressive corporate income tax rates to taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 10%, 20%, 22%, and 25% brackets in the same way for resident and non-resident corporations. If the entity is a foreign corporation's Korean branch, the branch taxable income is entered and the local income tax surtax on the national corporate income tax is assessed in the companion local income tax return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-exempt or tax-reduced income adjustments, tax deductions, R&D credits, foreign tax credits, and audit assessments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claiming a foreign tax credit for foreign-source anti-cheat software licensing income requires documentary proof of foreign taxes paid. Treaty-based deductions and credits must not be claimed directly on this line by the non-resident shareholder because dividend and royalty withholding is a separate procedure. Ensure the R&D credit claim is supported by technical staff logs, source code records, and payroll allocated to qualifying software development.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepaid Corporate Income Tax, interim prepayments made during the current year, and withholding tax credits already collected from Korean payers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When the Korean anti-cheat engine company receives payments from a non-resident licensee without Korean withholding, include the gross amount and make an adjustment for foreign taxes paid at source. Verify that any foreign tax credit cap has been calculated under the Korean limitation and that carryover credits do not exceed the applicable 5-year horizon.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction disclosure schedule providing detail of domestic and cross-border intercompany transactions, counterparties, transfer pricing methodology, and supporting documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose each licensing, royalty, service, and trademark arrangement with the non-resident related party. Attach the Local File and Master File if the aggregate cross-border related-party transaction amount exceeds KRW 10 billion. For anti-cheat engine licensing, use the tested-party net profit indicator under the TNMM or a comparable CUP analysis; explicitly state why the selected method is the best method and provide the interquartile range.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net Corporate Income Tax Payable, refund amount, and the representative director's signed declaration that the return is complete and correct.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The representative director of the Korean Chusik Hoesa must verify that outbound dividends, royalties, and interest have been subjected to the domestic withholding tax unless treaty relief was properly approved. Signing this declaration with knowledge of a sham IP holding arrangement or fraudulent conduit will expose the director to personal civil and criminal liability; the National Tax Service may blacklist the director, issue a travel ban, and freeze personal assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the corporate income tax return attracts a penalty of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax where no return is filed, and underreporting penalties of 10% or 20% of the underpaid tax depending on the degree of concealment. Unpaid corporate income tax accrues a daily additional tax of approximately 0.03% from the original due date until fully paid. Fraudulent evasion is prosecuted under the Punishment for Tax Evasion Act, carrying imprisonment of up to 10 years or a fine not exceeding twice the amount of tax evaded.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory withholding tax on dividends remitted to a non-resident shareholder is 20% national corporate income tax withholding plus 2% local income tax, an aggregate statutory rate of 22% on the gross dividend.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding under an applicable Double Tax Treaty, the non-resident payee must file an application to the National Tax Service before or at the time of payment, together with a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty jurisdiction, a beneficial ownership certificate confirming actual entitlement to the dividend, and evidence that the recipient has no Korean permanent establishment to which the dividend is attributable. The Korean withholding agent must retain a certified copy of the approved treaty relief application. If the TRC is not obtained before payment, the payer must withhold at the statutory 22% rate and the payee may seek a post-payment refund through year-end assessment after presenting the required treaty documents and proving that the recipient is not a conduit entity.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to a non-resident for the use of software or anti-cheat technology are subject to a statutory aggregate rate of 22%, generally reduced to 10% under most Korean income tax treaties. Interest paid to a non-resident lender is subject to the same 22% statutory aggregate rate, with treaty rates typically ranging from 10% to 15%. Treaty reductions are available only where the non-resident recipient is the beneficial owner, has no Korean permanent establishment, submits the required TRC, and complies with the Korean withholding exemption procedure.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion aggregate cross-border related-party transactions in the preceding business year triggers mandatory Local File preparation; Master File preparation is also required where the multinational group has consolidated revenue exceeding approximately KRW 1 trillion and cross-border related-party transactions are present.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply a formal Economic Substance Regulation as in certain offshore jurisdictions, but the National Tax Service applies a substance-over-form doctrine, anti-conduit principles, and Controlled Foreign Corporation rules under the International Tax Adjustment Act. A Korean anti-cheat engine company must demonstrate actual personnel, decision-making, server activity, R&D execution, and core income-generating activity in Korea; otherwise, the tax authority may recharacterize royalty flows, deny treaty benefits, and treat offshore IP holding companies as sham entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - Understatement of Digital Asset and Licensing Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Chusik Hoesa sells kernel-level anti-cheat engine licenses to non-resident game operators but deliberately records the revenue as a deductible consulting or service fee paid to a tax-haven intermediary while no actual consulting services are rendered outside Korea, shifting taxable profits offshore and reducing Korean corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Punishment for Tax Evasion Act Article 9, persons who deliberately conceal taxable income are subject to imprisonment of up to 10 years or a fine not exceeding twice the amount of tax evaded; the Corporate Tax Act also imposes a 20% under-reporting penalty and 0.03% daily delay surcharge on the unpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director may be personally liable for the unpaid corporate tax through piercing the corporate veil when the intermediary structure is found to be fictitious. The National Tax Service may blacklist the director, issue a travel ban, freeze personal bank accounts, seize personal assets, and the director may face criminal imprisonment if fraudulent intent is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation and Arm's Length Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The company engages in cross-border related-party transactions involving IP royalties, licensing, or anti-cheat technology transfers with a foreign parent or affiliated IP holding company but fails to prepare and file the Local File and Master File, fails to perform a comparability analysis, and uses an unsubstantiated royalty rate outside the interquartile arm's length range.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Tax Adjustment Act, the Korean tax authority may adjust the taxable income by using the arm's length price and impose a transfer pricing penalty of 20% of the understated corporate income tax, plus daily delay surcharge for tax underpayment; failure to submit documentation may also trigger documentation penalties and extend the assessment statute of limitations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the intercompany pricing and directed the transfer pricing policy may be held personally responsible if the pricing arrangement was willfully manipulated. Criminal prosecution for tax evasion can result in imprisonment up to 10 years, and civil restitution of unpaid tax plus interest can be enforced directly against the personal assets of the responsible director upon piercing the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Treaty Abuse, Conduit Structures, and Beneficial Ownership Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean entity pays a dividend or royalty to an intermediate company in a low-tax treaty jurisdiction that has no employees, no office, no economic activity, and no core income-generating activities, and the intermediate company immediately passes the funds to a shareholder in another country while the Korean payer falsely certifies the intermediate company as the beneficial owner solely to obtain a reduced treaty withholding rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Tax Adjustment Act and the framework for prevention of treaty abuse, the National Tax Service will deny treaty benefits, re-source the payment to the actual beneficial owner, and impose the full 22% statutory withholding tax on the gross remittance together with under-withholding penalties and daily delay surcharge. Criminal sanctions for false statement to obtain improper tax treaty benefits include imprisonment for up to 5 years and fines under the Punishment for Tax Evasion Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed or directed the fraudulent treaty relief application are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid withholding tax, penalties, and interest. Korean courts may disregard the shareholder limited liability structure, blacklist the directors from international travel, order repatriation of diverted assets, and imprisonment of directors may be imposed where the conduit arrangement is found to be a deliberate tax evasion scheme.
